name.text: Finding the mistake in a sampling solution

questiontext.text:
Kiprono maximised \(P = {@pp@}x + {@pq@}y\) on the region R given by {@E[1]@}, with \(x\) and \(y\) whole numbers. His working:

Step 1: The vertices of R are {@E[3]@}.

Step 2: \(P\) at the vertices is {@E[4]@}.

Step 3: {@E[5]@}

Step 4: The greatest value is {@E[6]@}.

(a) Which statement describes his mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) What is the greatest value of \(P\) with whole numbers? [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) {@otext(keyv)@}

(b) A vertex that is not a whole-number point is not an answer: test the whole-number points of R around the best vertex, and check every constraint. The best is \(({@bst[1]@}, {@bst[2]@})\), with \(P = {@t@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: finding the mistake in a sampling solution

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (c) / Essential 1.4 (c): Read a worked sampling solution for a whole-number linear programming problem, name its mistake, and give the right maximum.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

node.description: His answer or the value at the vertex

truefeedback.text:
[[if test='is(abs(ans2 - sv) < 1/1000)']]

That is Kiprono's answer, which has the mistake.

[[else]]

That is the value at the vertex, which is not a whole-number point.

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Test the whole-number points of R near the best vertex and work out \(P\) at each.

qtest.description: Another mistake; value at the vertex
